section_summary: This section finishes a classified biographical and intelligence-service chronology of Japanese military attaché Makoto Onodera, then presents postwar diplomatic and investigative records concerning alleged Japanese agents, propagandists, collaborators, and military advisers. Major groups concern the disputed identity and activities of Eijiro Yoshimoto in Manchuria, Lieutenant General Saito's possible service with Chinese Communist forces, and extensive evidence that American citizen Posey Wellington Reeves performed paid propaganda work for Japan. The closing documents are 1946 telegrams about Gösta Guston, SKF's former representative in Japan, proposed travel to Washington, SKF's German holdings, and possible immunity from antitrust proceedings.

subfiles.title: Chronology of Major General Makoto Onodera's military and intelligence career
subfiles.to: Allied occupation and military intelligence authorities
subfiles.about: Continues a classified chronology of Makoto Onodera's assignments, contacts, intelligence sources, and political operations from the early 1930s through his 1946 interrogation.
subfiles.summary: The report traces Onodera's General Staff, teaching, Manchurian, Riga, China, and Stockholm assignments, naming superior officers, colleagues, foreign military contacts, intelligence sources, and agents. It describes border reconnaissance against the Soviet Union, cooperation with Latvian and Estonian intelligence, political intelligence work in China, and his accreditation in Scandinavia. The chronology ends with his January 1946 repatriation and interrogation at Sugamo Prison from May through July 1946.

subfiles.title: Forwarding of German lists of Japanese friends of the Nazi government
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards two captured German Foreign Office lists identifying Japanese favored by the Nazi government.
subfiles.summary: Forwards German lists, captured in Berlin, of Japanese proposed for decorations for Tripartite Pact services and of prominent German-Japanese Comradeship members.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning alleged broadcasts by J. W. van Dienst
subfiles.about: Responds to the Netherlands request for evidence of J. W. van Dienst's alleged pro-Japanese radio activity.
subfiles.summary: The Department reports that United States authorities found no record of broadcasts or other pro-Japanese activities by van Dienst. It offers to conduct a further search if the Netherlands supplies details of his capture, present detention, and custodial authority.

subfiles.title: Netherlands request for evidence against J. W. van Dienst
subfiles.about: Requests American evidence for possible collaboration proceedings against alleged Japanese broadcaster J. W. van Dienst.
subfiles.summary: The note states that van Dienst was employed to broadcast over Japanese radio before and during the war. The Netherlands asks for reports or affidavits because records held in the Netherlands East Indies were destroyed during the Japanese invasion of 1942.

subfiles.title: Further information concerning Eijiro Yoshimoto
subfiles.from: Angus Ward, American consul general, Mukden
subfiles.to: J. Leighton Stuart, American ambassador, Nanking
subfiles.about: Reports an investigation into Eijiro Yoshimoto, an alleged Japanese Foreign Office representative arrested in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Ward concludes Eijiro Yoshimoto was probably an impostor and opportunist, possibly Korean, not a Foreign Office official; suggests confidential consultation with Colonel McFadden.

subfiles.title: External Survey Detachment investigation of Eijiro Yoshimoto
subfiles.from: Security Officer, External Survey Detachment 44 D, United States Navy
subfiles.about: Summarizes prisoner interviews and record checks concerning Yoshimoto's identity, career claims, aliases, imprisonment, and misconduct.
subfiles.summary: Survey Detachment report: Yoshimoto's claims of Tokyo Imperial University and Foreign Office service were contradictory; prisoners thought him Korean; alias Sonoda, alleged Communist collaboration and relief-fund misuse.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Lieutenant General Saito's possible Communist advisory role
subfiles.about: Reports that retired Japanese Lieutenant General Saito may be serving as a military adviser to Chinese Communist forces.
subfiles.summary: Source says Lt. Gen. Saito retired in 1943, headed a Manchurian agricultural company, never commanded the Hwalong Army, and was later reportedly sent to Mudanjiang as a Communist adviser.

subfiles.title: Transmittal concerning Posey Wellington Reeves
subfiles.to: Attorney General and Foreign Agents Registration Section, Department of Justice
subfiles.about: Transmits the State Department's memorandum and enclosures concerning Posey Wellington Reeves.
subfiles.summary: Cover sending the Reeves material to the Attorney General and Foreign Agents Registration Section for information and possible action.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Posey Wellington Reeves
subfiles.from: Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Jack D. Neal
subfiles.about: Evaluates Reeves's concealed pro-Japanese activities and recommends recalling his passport.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Reeves planned to assist Laurel in the Philippines; captured Embassy archives show over forty letters of assistance to Japan, 1937-41. Evidence was insufficient for FARA action; passport recall recommended and FBI notified.

subfiles.title: Comparison of Reeves's 1946 statements with his letters to the Japanese Embassy
subfiles.to: State Department, FBI, and Justice Department reviewers
subfiles.about: Contrasts Reeves's denials and minimizing statements with prewar letters documenting his pro-Japanese propaganda work and demands for payment.
subfiles.summary: The exhibit juxtaposes Reeves's 1946 explanations with his correspondence to Ambassador Hiroshi Saito and other Japanese officials. His letters show that he denounced China after the bombing of the President Hoover, repeatedly offered his services to Japan, traveled there with Japanese support, delivered speeches and international broadcasts, and disseminated pro-Japanese material in the United States. Extensive quoted correspondence documents his supervision by Kawai, Tsuchiya, and Kumasaki, disputes over expenses, and demand for $6,000 in compensation. The final comparison contradicts Reeves's claims that he rarely visited the Japanese Embassy and had done nothing to help Japan.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Posey Wellington Reeves
subfiles.from: Jack D. Neal, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.to: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Sends the Reeves memorandum and enclosure to the FBI for information and appropriate action.
subfiles.summary: Neal forwards the Division's Reeves memorandum to the FBI, leaving investigative action to it.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for Navy memorandum on Posey Reeves
subfiles.about: Records the charging out of an August 19, 1947 Navy memorandum concerning Posey Reeves.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip (894.20200/8-1947) for a Navy memorandum on Posey Reeves, charged February 19, 1951.

subfiles.title: Navy forwarding memorandum on Posey William Reeves
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations, William Abbott
subfiles.to: F41L1, attention Lieutenant T. G. Donahue
subfiles.about: Forwards a Navy summary responding to a request for information on Posey William Reeves.
subfiles.summary: Navy forwards its summary on Posey Reeves, requested August 5, 1947, for retention.

subfiles.title: Navy intelligence summary on Posey William Reeves
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.about: Summarizes biographical, employment, travel, and pro-Japanese activity attributed to Posey William Reeves.
subfiles.summary: Navy summary: Texas-born writer Reeves worked for Congress members and McNutt, allegedly tried to sell confidential plans, and did Japanese Foreign Office propaganda in 1938, keeping Embassy ties.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Reeves material to the American Mission in Manila
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Manila
subfiles.about: Forwards the August 7 Reeves memorandum because Reeves appeared to intend to visit the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Department sends the Manila mission the Reeves memorandum, noting he likely planned to travel to the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 103 urging instructions in the SKF case
subfiles.about: Urges Washington to issue instructions promptly concerning the SKF matter described in Stockholm telegram No. 102.
subfiles.summary: Ravndal, referring to Telegram No. 102, asks the Department to get instructions in the SKF case as soon as possible.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 126 on Treasury review of the SKF case
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains Treasury delays and asks that Guston remain in Stockholm pending a decision on investigating SKF holdings.
subfiles.summary: Department says it pressed Treasury for six weeks, recommended sending a Treasury investigator to examine SKF's German holdings in a Gothenburg bank, and advises Guston to remain in Stockholm meanwhile.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 102 on Gösta Guston's proposed SKF negotiations
subfiles.from: Christian M. Ravndal, American Legation, Stockholm
subfiles.about: Reports Guston's plan to travel to Washington with authority to negotiate settlement of charges against SKF.
subfiles.summary: Guston said SKF was frustrated by lack of specific charges but would open records and allow inspection of German shares in a Gothenburg safe-deposit box. He also claimed Allied espionage and wartime Schweinfurt targeting work.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Stockholm telegram No. 102
subfiles.about: Provides a security paraphrase of telegram No. 102 concerning Guston and SKF.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase repeats Guston's offer to bring records, negotiate all charges, and permit inspection of SKF's German holdings in Gothenburg. It also restates his claims concerning Allied espionage, MacArthur, Grew, wartime bombing intelligence, American family connections, and intended citizenship.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 255 requesting guidance on Guston's Washington trip
subfiles.about: Requests guidance on whether Guston should travel as SKF's representative and whether he might face antitrust detention.
subfiles.summary: Guston asks whether Washington still wants him once Treasury answers; Hamberg feared Justice's Antitrust Division might detain him, so the legation asks for results of further pressure.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 413 on Guston's possible immunity
subfiles.about: Reports that Treasury had not decided whether Guston's trip was necessary but that Justice would grant immunity if an official trip were required.
subfiles.summary: Treasury still cannot say whether Guston must come; if SKF blocking continues State will press for his trip, and Justice indicated immunity would then be granted.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 487 on Guston's proposed personal travel
subfiles.about: Asks whether Guston may travel privately to California while awaiting further SKF instructions.
subfiles.summary: Guston wishes to leave March 24 for his fiftieth birthday with family in California and await instructions there.

subfiles.title: Instruction allowing Guston's personal visit without immunity
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: States that Guston may visit the United States personally but cannot receive immunity for that visit.
subfiles.summary: Neither State nor Treasury needs Guston now, so no objection to his visit; the legation must warn that immunity cannot be requested for personal travel and report his departure date.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 575 seeking immunity assurances for Guston
subfiles.about: Reports Guston's rescheduled April 7 departure and his request for assurance of immunity.
subfiles.summary: Guston missed his planned departure and now leaves April 7; he wants clarification on immunity.
